evals.name: trailmark-codebase-preauthorized
evals.prompt: Generate the App Store screenshots for Trailmark 2.1. The Xcode project is in evals/files/trailmark (copy it into your working folder first and work on the copy). Use an editorial light direction with the app's green accent, recreate the screens from the SwiftUI code, render iPhone and iPad, and include the header and search creatives. Don't ask me anything, just build it.
evals.expected_output: A brief citing TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2", a one-line plan instead of a question, an asset set built from assets/template with no TODO markers and a Source comment per screen builder, iPhone and iPad screenshots plus header/search creatives that pass check_assets.py, no Health-sync or Apple Watch overclaim, a fresh review, and a Result/Evidence/Uncertainty/Decision report.
expectations: The app brief lists iphone and ipad as platforms and cites TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2" in project.pbxproj as evidence
The run fetched Apple's screenshot specification page, or recorded that it fell back to the dated snapshot in references/apple-specs.md
Because the prompt pre-authorized the run, it stated the plan in one line and did not stop to ask a question
The asset set's src/ is a copy of assets/template/, src/config.js contains no 'TODO:' marker, and every screen builder has a '// Source:' comment naming a file in the fixture
scripts/render.py and scripts/check_assets.py were both run, and check_assets.py printed a PASS summary line
iphone-6.3/ holds 3 to 10 PNGs at 1206x2622 and ipad-13/ holds PNGs at 2064x2752, all RGB without alpha
creative/ holds header.png at 3840x1646 and search.png at 3840x2560
No frame or caption presents Apple Health sync as a working feature, and no frame shows an Apple Watch app
The app's accent #2F9E6B (or the colorset's value) is used as the in-screen tint or brand color
A reviewer separate from the builder checked the frames against references/apple-guidelines.md, or the report says the review ran inline because no Agent tool was available
The final report opens with a Result: line carrying COMPLETE or PARTIAL and the output folder

The report has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines; Evidence cites the check_assets.py summary, Uncertainty names the recreated screens to verify on a build, and Decision names the upload or commit approval
The report states that nothing was committed or uploaded

evals.name: brewlog-landing-page
evals.prompt: Here's our landing page: evals/files/brewlog-site/index.html. We don't have the code handy. Make App Store screenshots for Brewlog, iPhone only, a bold brand direction using the site's copper and roast colors, no creatives. Go ahead without asking.
evals.expected_output: Landing-page branch: screens grounded only on the page's two UI mocks (recipe list, pour timer), captions drawn from the page's own claims without its © line, iPhone screenshots that pass check_assets.py, and a report flagging that the screens come from marketing mocks rather than the app.
expectations: The app brief records the input as a landing page and derives the iPhone platform from the page text ('Available on iPhone' or 'for iPhone')
Every recreated screen matches one of the page's two UI mocks: the Recipes list or the pour timer
No frame recreates a tasting-notes screen or any other screen the page does not show
No caption contains a price, URL or © symbol
iphone-6.3/ holds PNGs at 1206x2622 and check_assets.py printed a PASS summary line
No creative/ assets were rendered, because the prompt excluded them
The copper (#c2652a) and roast (#3b2416) colors from the page's CSS appear in config.js brand tokens
The report's Uncertainty: line says the screens are based on landing-page mocks and should be checked against, or replaced with, real captures
The final report opens with Result: and has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines

evals.name: trailmark-iphone-five-alternating
evals.prompt: Prepare the App Store visuals for Trailmark (the project is at evals/files/trailmark; work on a copy). iPhone only this time: five screenshots, alternating light and brand-colored frames, no creatives, and give me a preview I can look at. You have my go-ahead on the plan.
evals.expected_output: Exactly five iPhone frames in both iPhone classes with matching names, alternating canvas treatment, no iPad or creative output, a preview pointer, and the standard four-line report.
expectations: iphone-6.3/ and iphone-6.9/ each hold exactly 5 PNGs with identical file names, at 1206x2622 and 1320x2868
No ipad-13/ or creative/ files were rendered, because the user asked for iPhone only and no creatives
config.js alternates the canvas treatment across frames (for example dark: true on every other frame)
The first frame shows the trail log or another core screen, not settings
The run points to a preview: a published gallery page, or src/index.html opened without a query string, or the contact sheets
check_assets.py printed a PASS summary line
The final report opens with Result: and has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines

evals.name: approval-gate-stops
evals.prompt: Generate App Store screenshots for the app in evals/files/trailmark (work on a copy).
evals.expected_output: The run discovers the app and presents a plan with one combined question (direction, frames, UI source, extras), and writes no asset set before an answer. Ending without an answer, it reports BLOCKED with the pending question as the Decision.
expectations: The run produced an app brief (platforms iphone and ipad) before asking anything
The run asked one combined question covering direction, frame list, UI source and extras
No PNG and no src/ asset-set folder were written before the user answered
If the run ended without an answer, the report status is BLOCKED and its Decision: line names the pending question
